native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636 to -0.2293 (while becoming insignifcant) when both race and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: The effect of SES (socioeconomic status) on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636 to -0.2293 (while becoming insignificant) when both race and academic characteristics (standardized ability test scores and high school class rank) are included in the regression analysis.
native_result.WorkflowB:
1. Loaded and inspected nls_ses_processed.csv (8,773 observations, 9 variables).
2. Formulated baseline Logit models without academic variables to observe social background effects.
3. Formulated full Logit models incorporating race and academic characteristics (ABILITY composite and PERCENTILE IN CLASS).
4. Compared coefficient shifts across all candidate variables (SES, SAMPLE_SEX, FAMILY SIZE OF SAMPLE).
5. Confirmed SES uniquely exhibits the specified coefficient decline from positive (~0.36) to negative (~-0.23).
